candidate.answerReason: Independent fair tosses leave the sixth toss's heads probability at 1/2 regardless of the preceding five heads.

methods.label: Previous tosses do not change the next toss
methods.explanation: Each toss is independent. Previous outcomes do not change the probabilities of later outcomes, so the probability of heads on the 6th toss is still \(1/2\).
methods.levelReason: Uses the elementary independence interpretation already covered by Grade 9 probability misconceptions.
